headline: Indiana State Park Entrance and Nashville Village Access
reservation: Brown County State Park requires a daily entrance fee or an annual pass for all vehicles. During peak foliage in October, the town of Nashville and the park experience high demand; verify all accommodation bookings through official agency sites.

days.title: The Little Smokies Ridges

stops.name: Hesitation Point
stops.detail: Stop at this renowned overlook for a sweeping view of the forested hills and the park's varied terrain.

stops.name: Ogle Lake
stops.detail: Walk the perimeter trail of this serene reservoir, ideal for spotting waterfowl and early morning mist.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes; park roads are winding with low speed limits.
days.note: The West Gate entrance often experiences shorter queues than the North Gate during peak autumn weekends.

days.title: Heritage Arts and Historic Nashville
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Brown County State Park

stops.name: T.C. Steele State Historic Site
stops.detail: Tour the 'House of the Singing Winds' and the artist's gardens that inspired the local impressionist movement.

stops.name: Nashville Artist Colony
stops.detail: Explore the historic village center, visiting galleries that feature locally made pottery and woodwork.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; town parking is metered or in designated pay lots.
days.note: Most artisan shops in Nashville open at 10 AM; morning is the best time to find town parking.

days.title: Hidden Valleys and Yellowwood

stops.name: Yellowwood State Forest
stops.detail: Visit the quiet lake and explore the more rugged trails of this state forest for a secluded experience.

stops.name: Beanblossom Overlook
stops.detail: Capture views of the protected wetlands and the rolling topography north of Nashville.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; some roads to Yellowwood are gravel and can be narrow.
days.note: State forests have different regulations than state parks; verify hunting season dates before hiking.

intel.title: Nashville Village Parking
intel.text: Public parking is available in central lots behind the shops, but these fill early in October. Consider walking from local inns if staying within the village limits.

intel.title: Valley Dead Zones
intel.text: Expect total loss of GPS and cell signals in the deeper ravines of the state park. Keep a physical park map obtained from the gatehouse at all times.

intel.title: Nashville Hub Utility
intel.text: Fuel and electric charging stations are located in Nashville. The interior of Brown County State Park does not provide fuel services.

intel.title: Leaf-Peeping Peak
intel.text: Mid-to-late October is the busiest time for the region. Traffic on State Road 46 can move slowly; plan for extra travel time between Bloomington and Nashville.

intel.title: State Park Gates
intel.text: The North Gate features a historic covered bridge that has height and weight restrictions. Larger RVs should utilize the West Gate entrance on State Road 46.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Indianapolis International Airport (IND) and drive 75-90 minutes south to Nashville for village check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for all major sites, though RV owners must avoid the North Gate covered bridge due to clearance limits.
plan.goldenHour: West Lookout within the state park is a classic sunset location, though autumn crowds are significant.
